# method: not digitised from pixels: the specification-sheet web page draws this chart client-side with plotly.js, and the manufacturer's plotted data series are embedded in the page source as JSON (drupalSettings.frequency_response_charts[0].series, the <script type=application/json data-drupal-selector=drupal-settings-json> block); each series' x and y arrays were copied verbatim (121 points, 20 Hz to 20 kHz, 1/12-octave spacing as published, x values as given e.g. 21.1796875); SPL series are on plotly axis y (linear, 50..110 dB, 5 dB grid), impedance series on axis y2 (log, range 10^0.48..10^2.7 ohm), x axis log 10^1.3..10^4.3 Hz; series are matched to nominal impedance by the series name (e.g. 'P10R - 8 ohm') and the impedance series that follows it with the same line colour; no smoothing, interpolation or resampling was applied, so there are no extra points around the resonance peak

# notes: Impedance measured in free air (chart title "Free Air Impedance"). 1/12-octave sampling means the resonance peak may fall between points: the sampled maximum can under-read the true peak height and be up to 1/24 octave (2.9%) off in frequency. Chart title verbatim: "Frequency Response on IEC Baffle (DIN45575) @ 1W, 1 m - Free Air Impedance". Sheet sensitivity row verbatim: "Sensitivity@1W,1m" 4 ohm 95.1 dB, 8 ohm 94.2 dB, 16 ohm 94.7 dB. The sheet does not state the T/S measurement method, drive level or ambient conditions, nor the voltage behind "1W" (conventionally 2.83 V for 8 ohm, 2.0 V for 4 ohm, 4.0 V for 16 ohm). Uncertainty fields describe transcription only (values are the manufacturer's own numbers, given to 8+ significant figures); the measurement's own uncertainty is unstated. Curve key nominal= is the nominal impedance in ohm of the version measured. Sheet/curve inconsistency: high-Qms driver (Qms 15-24), the sampled peak under-reads Re+Res (4 ohm 50.6 vs 62.8; 8 ohm 83.5 vs 108.7; 16 ohm 108.6 vs 161.3 ohm) because of 1/12-octave sampling; 8 ohm column Res 102 is inconsistent with Re*Qms/Qes = 54.4 ohm (Bl^2/Res gives Qms 27.8 vs printed 14.83).
